payload.answer: [hard] Every change carries a before/after measurement committed as evidence. A performance change with no number attached is not a performance change. [hard] Correctness is never traded for speed. All 7 gates stay green, including 100% branch coverage per layer -- a faster system that drops a job or double-counts spend is a regression regardless of the benchmark. [hard] The ledger stays append-only and the queue stays PostgreSQL; no caching layer that can serve stale budget data, since the budget brake is a safety mechanism and a stale read there spends real money. [hard] domain/ stays pure. [hard] No micro-optimisation without a measured win -- if it does not move a number, it does not land. This is a deliberate optimisation push, not licence to churn. [soft] Prefer pushing filters into SQL over adding indexes; prefer adding an index over adding a cache. [hard] Conventional Commits, feature branch into develop.
